title: Majority Element (>n/2 times)
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Find the element that appears more than n/2 times (guaranteed to exist).
intuition: Pair off two different elements and discard both. A strict majority cannot be fully cancelled, so whatever survives is the candidate. That is Boyer-Moore voting in one sentence.

approaches.title: Brute: count each element
Better: hash map counts
approaches.idea: One pass to count, one to pick.

approaches.title: Optimal: Boyer-Moore voting
approaches.idea: One candidate + one counter; verify at the end if existence is not guaranteed.
approaches.whyWorks: Every decrement destroys one majority and one non-majority occurrence. With > n/2 copies the majority cannot be exhausted first.

specialTechnique.title: Boyer-Moore majority vote
specialTechnique.body: Cancel unequal pairs. Generalises to > n/k by keeping k-1 candidates (see Majority Element n/3).

edgeCases: No majority exists -> verification pass matters
commonMistakes: Skipping the verification pass when existence is not guaranteed
Resetting count without also resetting the candidate
patternRecognition: "More than n/k times" -> keep k-1 candidates and verify
followUps: What if you need all elements above a frequency threshold?
interviewInsight: Interviewers usually drop the existence guarantee to see whether you still verify.
